full_description: Learn how to design professional, responsive and interactive digital interfaces using Figma. This practical Figma UI Design & Responsive Prototyping course develops hands-on skills in interface layout, visual hierarchy, spacing systems, typography, wireframes, responsive design, component libraries and interactive prototypes. Master Figma's Auto Layout capabilities, including horizontal, vertical and grid layouts; Hug Contents, Fill Container, Fixed sizing, min/max dimensions, wrapping and nested component behavior. Learn to create adaptable website structures, responsive product cards, desktop and mobile navigation patterns, reusable UI components, variants, design styles and design tokens. Develop foundational knowledge of accessibility, contrast, target sizing, readable typography and consistent interaction states. Build practical skills in designing multi-screen e-commerce interfaces, mobile app flows, navigation interactions, overlays, interactive components and realistic prototype demonstrations. Explore Figma variables, reusable design libraries, light/dark modes and documented UI systems that support consistent design across multiple screens. Learn how to prepare organized design files, reusable assets, component specifications, responsive behavior notes and developer-ready handoff documentation. Complete a professional portfolio containing a responsive e-commerce website, a mobile app flow with at least five meaningful screens, a reusable component library, a clickable prototype and a documented developer handoff. The programme emphasizes genuine responsive behavior, professional interface craftsmanship, systematic component reuse and practical UI delivery. It is a focused UI production specialization, not a replacement for a longer programme covering comprehensive UX research, usability testing and product strategy.

faq.question: What is Figma UI Design & Responsive Prototyping?
faq.answer: Figma UI Design & Responsive Prototyping is an intensive 8-week, 64-hour practical specialization focused on interface design, Auto Layout mechanics, responsive web layouts, mobile app flows, component systems, design tokens, interactive prototyping, and developer handoff. Students learn to build interfaces that genuinely adapt across screen widths, graduating with a verified commercial UI portfolio backed by editable Figma source files.

faq.question: Is this Figma course suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes, this course is designed for beginners including aspiring UI designers, graphic designers entering digital product design, web designers, and frontend beginners. Training starts with fundamental UI principles—visual hierarchy, 8-point spacing grids, typography, and Figma workspace basics—before advancing to complex Auto Layout and component systems.

faq.question: What is the duration and fee?
faq.answer: The course duration is 8 Weeks (64 guided learning hours across 6 modules), and the tuition fee is ₹9,900. Nova Skills maintains a transparent pricing policy with 0% fake discounts, no artificial comparison pricing, and no countdown timers.

faq.question: Do I need coding knowledge?
faq.answer: No programming or coding knowledge is required. All core coursework, Auto Layout exercises, component design, and prototyping are executed visually within Figma Design and FigJam. However, the course teaches developer handoff principles so you understand how your designs translate cleanly into HTML, CSS, and frontend frameworks.

faq.question: Will I learn website and mobile app UI design?
faq.answer: Yes. The curriculum covers both responsive web interfaces (desktop, tablet, and mobile web layouts) and native mobile application screen flows (incorporating mobile touch targets, navigation patterns, and app states).

faq.question: What is Auto Layout in Figma?
faq.answer: Auto Layout is Figma's powerful layout engine that mimics modern CSS flexbox and grid behavior. It allows frames and components to grow, shrink, wrap, and reorder automatically based on content and container dimensions, forming the foundation of modern responsive interface design.

faq.question: Will I learn Hug, Fill and Fixed sizing?
faq.answer: Yes, mastering Hug Contents, Fill Container, and Fixed dimensions is a core technical milestone. You will learn exactly when and how to apply each sizing constraint, along with min/max width and height bounds, to ensure nested elements behave predictably during viewport resizing.

faq.question: Will I learn responsive website design?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn to construct responsive website structures that reflow gracefully across screen sizes, adapting multi-column product grids, card layouts, content sections, and navigation systems without horizontal overflow or broken elements.

faq.question: Can Figma layouts resize when frame width changes?
faq.answer: Yes. Using Figma Design's Auto Layout, constraints, Fill Container settings, and min/max dimensions, frames and nested components dynamically expand, contract, and wrap as the parent frame width is resized manually.

faq.question: Can a desktop menu automatically become a hamburger menu?
faq.answer: In standard Figma Design, continuous frame dragging does not automatically swap component variants between desktop links and a mobile hamburger icon; that structural breakpoint change is accomplished using configured component variants, documented breakpoint frames, or interactive prototypes. The course clearly teaches the distinction between continuous responsive reflow and structural variant switching.

faq.question: What is the difference between Figma Design responsiveness and Figma Sites breakpoints?
faq.answer: Figma Design uses Auto Layout and constraints for fluid resizing within frames, while structural breakpoint changes require explicit variant configurations. Figma Sites (where available) supports defined CSS-style breakpoints that automatically switch responsive component variants at specific viewport thresholds. The course teaches both concepts accurately.

faq.question: Will I learn responsive product cards and grids?
faq.answer: Yes. You will complete dedicated hands-on labs engineering responsive product cards with dynamic text wrapping, fixed image aspect ratios, and multi-column product grids that reflow smoothly across desktop, tablet, and mobile viewports.

faq.question: Will I learn Figma components and variants?
faq.answer: Yes. You will master main components, instances, component sets, and variants across multiple interaction states (default, hover, pressed, focus, disabled), along with component properties such as boolean toggles, text fields, and instance swap slots.

faq.question: Does the course cover design tokens and variables?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn to set up Figma variables for colors, numbers, and strings, organizing them into collections and distinguishing primitive tokens (raw values) from semantic tokens (functional design roles like background-primary or text-secondary).

faq.question: Will I learn light/dark mode design?
faq.answer: Yes. You will build a dual-theme UI system using Figma variable modes, demonstrating how an entire multi-screen interface instantly switches between Light and Dark themes through semantic token mapping.

faq.question: Will I create interactive prototypes?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 5 is dedicated to interactive prototyping. You will connect multi-screen flows, configure click/hover triggers, implement modal and drawer overlays, and animate state transitions using Smart Animate.

faq.question: How many mobile app screens will I design?
faq.answer: You will design a complete, cohesive mobile app user journey comprising at least five high-fidelity screens: Home feed, Search/Browse with filters, Product Detail, Cart/Saved Items, and Checkout Confirmation.

faq.question: Will I create a responsive e-commerce website?
faq.answer: Yes. Portfolio Project 01 requires building a fully responsive commercial e-commerce website featuring Homepage, Product Listing Page (PLP), and Product Detail Page (PDP) tested across desktop, tablet, and mobile viewports.

faq.question: What is Figma Dev Mode?
faq.answer: Figma Dev Mode is a dedicated workspace for developers to inspect design measurements, copy CSS and token values, view component properties, compare versions, and download production-ready assets. The course covers Dev Mode workflows alongside manual handoff methods.

faq.question: Will I learn developer handoff?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn how to prepare professional developer handoff specifications, including organized frame naming, layout and spacing annotations, CSS token documentation, exportable SVG assets, and design QA checklists.

faq.question: Does the course cover Figma Make and Figma Sites?
faq.answer: Yes, Figma Make (for AI-assisted prototype exploration) and Figma Sites (for breakpoint-based web layout demonstrations) are introduced as supporting capabilities where accessible, while keeping core manual UI craftsmanship in Figma Design as the primary focus.

faq.question: Do I need a paid Figma plan?
faq.answer: No. All core learning outcomes, Auto Layout exercises, component systems, and portfolio deliverables are fully achievable using a standard free Figma account alongside instructor demonstrations of advanced features.

faq.question: What portfolio projects will I build?
faq.answer: You will complete four primary portfolio deliverables: (1) Responsive E-commerce Website UI (Homepage, PLP, PDP), (2) Five-Screen Mobile App Flow, (3) Reusable UI Component Library with Design Tokens & Light/Dark Modes, and (4) Clickable Prototype & Developer Handoff Package.

faq.question: Is this a complete UX research programme?
faq.answer: No. Course 51 is a focused UI production and responsive prototyping specialization. While it covers screen architecture, wireframes, and basic user flows, comprehensive UX research methodologies, user interviews, and product strategy belong to the extended UI/UX Design Professional programme.

faq.question: What is the difference between this course and UI/UX Design Professional?
faq.answer: Course 51 focuses deeply on hands-on UI execution in Figma—Auto Layout, responsive screens, design tokens, component variants, prototypes, and developer handoff (8 weeks, 64 hours). UI/UX Design Professional is a longer, broader qualification covering extensive UX research, usability testing, and product strategy.

faq.question: Is this an official Figma certification?
faq.answer: No. This is an industry-recognized professional certification issued by Nova Skills Education Institute validating practical Figma UI design and responsive prototyping craftsmanship. It is not an official corporate certification from Figma Inc.

faq.question: What entry-level career opportunities can I explore?
faq.answer: Graduates can explore entry-level opportunities such as Junior UI Designer, Figma UI Designer, Responsive Web Designer, Mobile App UI Assistant, UI Component Designer, and Developer Handoff Design Assistant.
